gifts.title: Build the real Day By Day website — theirs currently says 'Demo'
gifts.for_complaint: No real website / online ordering is broken or doesn't exist
gifts.deliverable: A one-page site (handed over as an HTML file + hosted URL) built from what's actually true about this exact restaurant: real hours pulled from their OSM listing (Mo-Sa 6-3, Su 7-3), phone, address, a plain 'Yes, we are open' line answering the live Jan 2026 closure rumor, a reconstructed menu of their actual named dishes pulled from 500 reviews (biscuits and gravy, buckwheat pancakes, corned beef hash, Cubano, Rachel, patty melt, eggs benedict, salmon scramble), the koi-pond dog-friendly patio, a note that the patio entrance is around back near the kitchen (a repeat point of confusion), and the payment note below.
gifts.inputs_needed: Current daybydaymn.com site is live at a 'Demo' placeholder — no login needed to observe it, only to replace it. OSM gives hours/phone/address (public, reachable now). Menu items are reconstructed from review text, not an official price sheet, so prices are omitted; a photo of their real posted menu would sharpen this but isn't required to ship v1.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Their own domain has been showing visitors the word 'Demo' while a live Google review says they're closing and staff themselves told a customer 'we don't have a website to order from' — three symptoms of one root cause, fixable with one page, no account needed to build it.

gifts.title: A 'seat yourself' sign that actually tells people what happens next
gifts.for_complaint: Customers ignored after self-seating / slow or rude service
gifts.deliverable: A printable host-stand sign and matching table tent (PDF/PNG, print at home or at any copy shop) with one line: 'Seat yourself anywhere — a server will greet you within 5 minutes. Waving gets our attention fastest if we're slammed.' Directly answers the two documented failure cases: the seat-yourself sign with no follow-through, and staff distracted on phones near a waiting table.
gifts.inputs_needed: None beyond their name, already public. No menu, no login, no paid printing service required — file is print-ready as-is.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: The exact complaint ('the sign said seat yourself... I waited 5 min and no one served me') shows up multiple times across three years; the sign itself is the gap, not the staff.

gifts.title: A payment sign so nobody's surprised at checkout
gifts.for_complaint: Payment methods outdated / confusing (Visa-only, no tap, cash-vs-card price gap)
gifts.deliverable: A small printable sign for the register/front door: 'We currently accept cash and Visa. No tap/contactless yet. Paying cash saves you our card processing fee.' Removes the guesswork three separate 2025 reviewers hit at the point of paying.
gifts.inputs_needed: The exact cash-discount percentage isn't public; the sign is written to work without it ('saves you our card processing fee') so it's accurate without needing their POS settings.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Three different customers in one year hit this exact surprise at checkout — a $0 sign fixes a recurring bad last-impression moment.
